item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 291122
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Thu Oct 29 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Vance, located a couple hundred miles west-northwest of Cabo
Corrientes, Mexico.

Well Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
A broad area of low pressure is likely to develop well to the
southeast of the Hawaiian Islands this weekend or early next week.
Thereafter, environmental conditions appear generally favorable for
some slow development of this system as it moves westward to
west-northwestward into the Central Pacific basin.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Public Advisory Number 33
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM MST Thu Oct 29 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 291431
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Vance Advisory Number  33
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
800 AM MST Thu Oct 29 2026
 
...FLOOD AND MUDSLIDE THREAT CONTINUES FOR MEXICO DUE TO VANCE...
...MOISTURE FROM VANCE WILL SPREAD INTO PORTIONS OF THE
SOUTH-CENTRAL AND SOUTHWESTERN UNITED STATES...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM MST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...21.6N 108.8W
ABOUT 215 MI...350 KM WNW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
ABOUT 115 MI...185 KM SE OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...N OR 350 DEGREES AT 8 MPH...13 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1004 MB...29.65 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests along the west-central and northwestern coasts of Mexico
and the southern Baja California Peninsula should monitor the
progress of Vance.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM MST (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Vance was
located near latitude 21.6 North, longitude 108.8 West. Vance is
moving toward the north near 8 mph (13 km/h) and this motion is
expected to continue until Vance dissipates tonight or early Friday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 40 mph (65 km/h) with higher gusts.
Weakening is forecast, and Vance is expected to become a
post-tropical remnant low later today.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 90 miles (150 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1004 mb (29.65 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
RAINFALL: Through tonight, Vance is expected to produce 2 to 4
inches of rain across central and southern Sinaloa, far southwestern
Durango, and far northwestern Nayarit, with isolated higher totals
over 5 inches possible across central and southern Sinaloa. This
rainfall may produce flooding and mudslides, especially in areas
along steep terrain.
 
Moisture carried northeastward from Vance combined with other
Pacific moisture will begin to produce heavy rainfall across the
U.S. Southern Plains and New Mexico today into Friday.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Vance,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Vance will affect coastal portions of
southwestern and west-central Mexico, as well as the southern
portion of the Baja California Peninsula, during the next day or
so. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Hagen
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Forecast Discussion Number 33
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM MST Thu Oct 29 2026 
542 
WTPZ42 KNHC 291432
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Storm Vance Discussion Number  33
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
800 AM MST Thu Oct 29 2026
 
Deep convection near the center yesterday evening produced 
tropical-storm-force winds in Vance's northern and eastern 
semicircles.  Strong (50 kt) west-southwesterly vertical wind shear 
has been pushing the deep convection farther and farther away from 
the center over the past 9 to 12 hours, and now the convection is 
located more than 90 n mi east and northeast of the center.  Recent 
surface observations from Islas Marias are 20 kt gusting to 30 kt 
while located underneath some of the deepest convection for the past 
few hours, so the winds are likely decreasing, but it is still 
possible that a small area of winds to tropical-storm-force exists 
in that convection, so Vance will be held at 35 kt for this 
advisory.  Scatterometer passes expected within the next couple of 
hours should give us a better assessment of Vance's strength.
 
The UW-CIMSS shear analysis and the latest SHIPS guidance are both 
analyzing about 50 kt of west-southwesterly vertical wind shear 
currently impacting Vance.  The shear is forecast to increase to 
around 55 kt over the next 6 h or so.  Vance is also located within 
a drier environment than it was yesterday, with mid-level relative 
humidity values in the 40 to 50 percent range. Therefore, deep 
convection, which is currently located well east of the center and 
moving farther away, is unlikely to return, and the GFS and ECMWF 
simulated satellite products do not forecast any new convection to 
form near the center.  Therefore, the timing of post-tropical 
transition has been moved up to hour 12 in the official forecast. 
Most of the models then show the remnant low dissipating in about 18 
to 24 hours over the southern Gulf of California.  Although gradual 
weakening is forecast until dissipation, gusts to 
tropical-storm-force are still likely today within the deep 
convection well east of the center.
 
Vance has been moving northward, or 350/7 kt.  A generally northward 
motion at about the same speed is expected until Vance degenerates 
into a trough of low pressure over the southern Gulf of California 
in about 18 to 24 hours.  The new NHC forecast is nudged a bit to 
the left of the previous one and is near the latest HCCA and GDMI. 
It should be emphasized that the main threat with Vance is the very 
heavy rainfall and high rain rates near the areas of very deep 
convection near the Islas Marias and west-central Mexico.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Periods of heavy rainfall associated with Vance will impact
portions of western Mexico during the next day or two. This rainfall
may produce flooding and mudslides across central and southern
Sinaloa, far southwestern Durango, and far northwestern Nayarit,
especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
2. Moisture carried northeastward from Vance will produce heavy rain
across portions of the U.S. Southern Plains and New Mexico today
into Friday.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  29/1500Z 21.6N 108.8W   35 KT  40 MPH
 12H  30/0000Z 22.9N 108.5W   25 KT  30 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 24H  30/1200Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Hagen
